body:
I attach a pcap.gz generated during run of TC_pfcp_heartbeat_timeout here.

[SMF_Tests.TC_pfcp_heartbeat_timeout.pcap.gz](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33337400/SMF_Tests.TC_pfcp_heartbeat_timeout.pcap.gz)

There the question is over all whether we consider "heartbeat timeout" scenario as a UPF failure and hence as as PFCP association tear down.

The answer seems to be yes, since failure to retransmit HB Request or any other message a number of times will change state of the FSM and re-trigger PFCP Association Setup procedure.

And then, from the PFCP specs one can infer that the PFCP sessions are bound to a specific (set of) PFCP associations. When the last of those PFCP associations between SMF<->UPF goes down, the sessions should be relesaed:

3GPP TS 29.244 5.22.3 With one PFCP association per SMF and UPF: (see specially last sentence)
> When an SMF is added or removed from the SMF set, e.g. during a scale-out or scale-in of the SMF set, this
> SMF shall establish or tear down its PFCP association with the UPF. When a PFCP association with a particular
> SMF is released (e.g. due to an SMF shutting down / scale-in of the SMF set), any PFCP sessions that were still
> served by this SMF shall be maintained by the SMF set and the UPF if there is at least one PFCP association
> remaining established between the UPF and another SMF of the SMF set. If so, the UPF shall move such PFCP
> sessions towards other SMF(s) of the SMF set (as described in this clause and clause 5.22.4). Otherwise, if the
>  PFCP association being released is the last PFCP association that was established between the UPF and any
> SMF of the SMF set, the PFCP sessions shall be deleted as specified in clauses 5.18 and 6.2.8.


3GPP TS 29.244  6.2.6 PFCP Association Setup Procedure
> The PFCP Association Setup procedure shall be used to setup a PFCP association between a CP function and a UP
> function, to enable the CP function to use the resources of the UP function subsequently, i.e. establish PFCP Sessions.


3GPP TS 29.244 6.2.6.2.1 CP Function Behaviour:
> The CP function shall initiate the PFCP Association Setup procedure to request to setup a PFCP association towards a
> UP function prior to establishing a first PFCP session on this UP function.
Note this same issue also probably affects open5gs-upfd.

issue.body:
The specs clearly state SEID must be zero in this case: """
3GPP TS 29.244 7.2.2.4.2 Conditions for Sending SEID=0 in PFCP Header If a peer's SEID is not available, the SEID field shall still be present in the header and its value shall be set to "0" in the following messages:
- PFCP Session Establishment Request message on Sxa/Sxb/Sxc/N4; """

Before this patch, open5gs-smfd (and probably also open5gs-swgc though I didn't check) were sending SEID!=0 (the previous existing SEID) during PFCP session restoration after Recovery Timestamp increase quicked in. This is wrong imho, because at that time the UPF is believed to be disassociated and hence PFCP Association Setup procedure is run before attempting PFCP session restoring. Which means, in practice, after a PFCP Association Setup the previous sessions (SEID) lose any kind of meaning, and hence they are all considered as not available.

body:
@pespin

Thanks for the update. I've applied a small follow-up to check that EPC sessions are in `smf_gsm_state_operational` before looking up the default bearer and sending Delete Bearer Request.

A failed Create Session Request—for example, due to UE IP allocation failure—can leave a session with a selected UPF but no bearer. A subsequent UPF heartbeat timeout would then hit `ogs_assert(linked_bearer)`. The state check prevents this and also skips sessions still being established or already being released.

I also moved the `linked_bearer` declaration to the beginning of the function and added an INFO log for skipped sessions.

Thanks again!

Sukchan

@acetcom thanks. I'll try to add some more TTCN-3 test triggering the PFCP Heartbeat timeout with some session in non-operational state, like before the PCCP Create Session Request was not yet answered.

Capture pack for the 5G procedure, as requested (cross-ref #4863):

https://github.com/zhangerfei-dp/open5gs/tree/capture-4860/captures

- `sn100-bridge-pfcp-ngap-sbi.pcap.gz` (2.1 MB) — primary capture, 5GC bridge, filtered to
  PFCP (`udp.port==8805`), N2 (`sctp`, AMF ↔ gNB, NGAP PPID 0x3c) and SBI (`tcp.port==7777`,
  TLS in our lab). Direct download:
  https://github.com/zhangerfei-dp/open5gs/raw/capture-4860/captures/sn100-bridge-pfcp-ngap-sbi.pcap.gz
- `ue-eth0.pcap.gz` — UE container interface: NAS over RLS (`udp.port==4997`): release command,
  reactivation, retries, rejects. Direct download:
  https://github.com/zhangerfei-dp/open5gs/raw/capture-4860/captures/ue-eth0.pcap.gz
- `pfcp-sequence.txt` — decoded PFCP message list for the whole window.
- `FLOW-STEPS.md` — the timeline with per-file notes and useful display filters.

Setup: live 5G SA core (open5gs main @ `26f9edd4` + `ae7a88a` on the SMF), eUPF data plane
(native XDP), UERANSIM gNB + 4 UEs × 2 PDU sessions = 8 sessions. Stimulus: `docker stop upf`,
leave it dead ~36 s, `docker start upf`. Times below are UTC.

SMF ↔ UPF (PFCP), the core of the scenario:

    09:22:25.794  Heartbeat REQ/RESP — last exchange before the stop
    09:22:30.798  Heartbeat REQ #1 — no response (UPF stopped at 09:22:30.0)
    09:22:33.301  Heartbeat REQ #2   (2.5 s cadence)
    09:22:35.804  Heartbeat REQ #3
    09:22:38.308  give-up: "No Heartbeat from UPF" -> "No UPF available"; the SMF then
                  retries Association Setup Requests towards the dead UPF (~every 1–2.5 s)
    09:23:06.314  Association Setup Request (UPF is back)
    09:23:07.318  Association Setup Response; heartbeats both ways
                  ("Remote PFCP restarted ... in Heartbeat REQ" -> "PFCP restoration")
    09:23:07.499  Session Establishment Request ×6 (the sessions that re-established) +
                  QER Session Modification requests, all within ~230 ms

Rest of the procedure (from NGAP/NAS in the capture and the component logs):

    09:22:38.47   UEs get PDU Session Release Command (5GSM cause = reactivation requested);
                  gNB releases the N2 resources (~09:22:38.47–39.49)
    09:22:38.75+  while the UPF is dead: UE re-establishment attempts rejected by the SMF
                  ("No UPFs are PFCP associated that are suited to RR"); UEs retry ~1/s
    09:23:07.5+   6/8 sessions re-established automatically after the UPF returned
                  (in two earlier runs of the same scenario: 8/8 within ~2–4 s)

Notes:
- SBI is TLS/mTLS in this deployment, so the N11/N10/N7 contents are encrypted in the capture;
  PFCP, NGAP (incl. the NAS PDU inside) and RLS/NAS are plaintext.
- There is also an unrelated SGW-C ↔ SGW-U PFCP pair in the file (`172.22.0.5 ↔ 172.22.0.6`);
  the SMF ↔ UPF traffic is `172.22.0.7 ↔ 172.22.0.8`.
- One oddity in this particular run (not root-caused, may be an artifact of our test sequence):
  one UE's two sessions did not re-establish — its attempts were answered with
  `No handler for event OGS_EVENT_NAME_SBI_SERVER` (gsm-sm.c:759) while the SMF still held
  stale session objects for it. A clean SMF restart cleared the state. Happy to dig further
  if that's interesting.
- If readable SBI payloads would help the TTCN-3 work, say the word and I'll re-run with SBI
  TLS disabled for a capture.

Happy to provide anything else that helps.

Thanks for #4863 and the follow-up. A few data points and one proposal from our side, mostly about what happens
*after* this change for deployments that would rather keep sessions across a short UPF outage.

**1. Detection time with the default timers (from reading the code on `ae7a88a9`)**

There is no dedicated knob for the N4 heartbeat; everything derives from `time.message.duration` (default 10 s),
`lib/app/ogs-config.c`:

- `no_heartbeat_duration = max(10 s, message.duration + 1 s)` = 11 s (`:409-411`); the timer is restarted on every
  heartbeat received (`lib/pfcp/handler.c:86-87`), and when it fires the SMF sends a Heartbeat Request.
- `t1_response_duration = message.duration / (3 + 1)` = 2.5 s, `n1_response_rcount` = 3 (`:388-393`); the request is
  sent 3 times and the transaction gives up after 3 × T1 = 7.5 s (`lib/pfcp/xact.c:630-650`), which raises
  `SMF_EVT_N4_NO_HEARTBEAT` → `reselect_upf()`.

So, after the UPF stops answering, sessions are now released somewhere between ~7.5 s and ~18.5 s, depending on
where in the heartbeat cycle the UPF died. That matches the 7.5 s between the first unanswered Heartbeat Request and
the give-up in @zhangerfei-dp's capture. Changing `time.message.duration` to get e.g. 60 s would also stretch all SBI
client timeouts (`:376-386`), so it is not really usable as a "UPF failure timeout".

For the restart case we measured, in a test harness with default timers (open5gs abts test that `kill -9`s the UPF and
starts it again), that the SMF detected the restart via the new Recovery Time Stamp after **11 s** in two runs and
**18 s** in two other runs, depending on the position in the heartbeat cycle. Until then the restarted UPF answers
session-level messages with "Cannot find PFCP-Node" and the SMF's Session Modification runs into its timeout. These
are test-harness numbers, not field numbers.

**2. Restoration vs. release is now decided by a race**

With #4863 the outcome of a UPF restart depends on timing rather than on configuration:

- the UPF is back and answers one of the three heartbeat transmissions → `restoration_required` → `pfcp_restoration()`
  re-establishes all PFCP sessions (`src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:465-506`), the UEs keep their PDU sessions;
- the UPF is back a little later → all sessions on that node are released (`reselect_upf()`, `src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:508-582`), each UE gets
  "reactivation requested" and starts re-establishing, which is rejected about once per second per UE while no UPF is
  associated (as seen in @zhangerfei-dp's test).

For a single-UPF site with a UPF that restarts in a few seconds (e.g. under systemd), both branches are reachable for
the very same failure. For voice users the second branch tears down every IMS PDU session, so the devices have
to set it up again and re-register, while the first branch is transparent to them.

**3. What the specs leave open**

TS 23.527 V18.6.0, clause 4.3.3:

> Procedures for PSA UPF failure without restart are implementation specific.

TS 23.527 V18.6.0, clause 4.5:

> If the N4 path to the UPF is down, the SMF should handle this as an UPF Failure without Restart, see clause 4.3.3.

TS 23.007 V18.5.0, clause 17.1A.4 (PGW-U Failure), NOTE:

> When a PGW-C detects the failure of a PGW-U without a restart, the PGW-C may select an alternative PGW-U to restore
> the Sx sessions in the UP function. How this is performed is implementation specific.

TS 23.527 V18.6.0, clause 4.3.2 (PSA UPF restart):

> Immediately after the re-establishment of a PFCP association between the SMF and the UPF, the SMF may start
> restoring PFCP sessions in the UPF.
> The SMF should prioritize the PFCP sessions to restore based on operator's policy.

On TS 29.244 clause 5.22.3 (quoted above): that clause starts with "If multiple PFCP associations are setup between an
UPF and the SMFs in an SMF set, the following applies:" (MPAS), and clause 6.2.8.1 frames the "last association →
delete the PFCP sessions" rule the same way ("When using the MPAS feature ..."). Deleting the PFCP sessions is also not
the same as releasing the PDU sessions: the restoration procedures above re-create the PFCP sessions for PDU sessions
that are kept. So I read the specs as allowing both "release" and "keep and restore" for the non-MPAS case, which is
also how the issue summarised it.

A precedent for making such a tear-down an operator choice is TS 23.007 V18.5.0, clause 17.1A.2 (PCRF failure, so a
different failure, quoted only as an analogy):

> ... the PGW may discard the request and may tear down the associated PDN connection, based on operator policy, by
> initiating a PGW initiated bearer deactivation procedure for the default bearer towards the MME/S4-SGSN with the
> cause set to "Reactivation requested". [...] Emergency and eMPS sessions should not be torn down.

**4. Proposal: make the reaction to a heartbeat timeout configurable**

Something along these lines (names are only a suggestion):

```yaml
smf:
  pfcp:
    upf_failure:
      action: release      # release | keep
      release_after: 0     # seconds after "No Heartbeat" before releasing; only with action: keep
```

- `release` (default, today's behaviour after #4863).
- `keep`: on `No Heartbeat` keep the SM contexts and keep trying to re-associate (as before #4863); when the
  association is re-established, run the restoration path. Since TS 23.527 4.2 says the Recovery Time Stamp in
  Association Setup is ignored, a returning UPF that lost its state is only recognised by the next heartbeat; with
  `keep` the SMF could restore unconditionally after re-association instead of waiting for `restoration_required`.
  `release_after` bounds the time during which the control plane assumes a working user plane, which addresses the
  accounting concern from the issue; when it expires, the existing release path from #4863 runs.
- Optionally, never release emergency sessions on this trigger (cf. 23.007 17.1A.2 above).

A separate knob for the N4 heartbeat interval/retries (instead of deriving it from `time.message.duration`) would make
`release_after` predictable as well.


**5. UPF side (re "this same issue also probably affects open5gs-upfd")**

On main, when the UPF loses the heartbeat towards the SMF it only goes back to `will_associate` and keeps all
sessions (`src/upf/pfcp-sm.c:342-345`); sessions of that SMF are removed only when the SMF comes back with a new
Recovery Time Stamp (`pfcp_restoration()`, `:371-386`). Here the spec is not implementation specific. TS 23.527 V18.6.0,
clause 4.4.3.1:

> When a UPF detects that a peer PFCP entity in the SMF is not reachable for a preconfigured time, and the MPAS or SSET
> procedure specified for SMF set in clause 5.22 of 3GPP TS 29.244 [4]) are not used, the UPF shall delete all the
> session contexts affected by the peer PFCP entity failure that it may have stored.

The "preconfigured time" can reasonably be longer than the heartbeat give-up, but some bound seems to be required.

**6. On the "No handler for event OGS_EVENT_NAME_SBI_SERVER" observation**

On `26f9edd4`/`ae7a88a9` that log line is in `src/smf/gsm-sm.c` at `:486` (`smf_gsm_state_initial`) and `:879`
(`smf_gsm_state_wait_5gc_sm_policy_association`), not at `:759`, so the tree in that test probably differs a bit.
`smf_gsm_state_wait_5gc_sm_policy_association` has no `OGS_EVENT_SBI_SERVER` case; only `initial` (`:342`),
`operational` (`:1214`), `wait_5gc_n1_n2_release` (`:3352`) and `5gc_session_will_deregister` (`:4143`) have one. If the
stale session was sitting in one of the other states, an Nsmf request for it would be logged like this and, as far as
we can see, not answered. We have not reproduced this; the state the session was in would tell.

Hi @MrBrownieCGN ,

1-
Regarding the timer timeouts, I agree they should be split into more fine grained values. In fact I already created ticket https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/issues/4876 to track it a few hours ago. Feel free to update that ticket with whatever proposal you think makes sense.
I don't plan to work on that myself for now since I'm now focusing/assigned on improving open5gs 5GC TTCN-3 coverage in osmo-ttcn3-hacks.git

2-
The race you mention is a derivate of "1.". With better fine-grained timeout values (ie. higher T_hearbeat timeout), the problem reduces a lot.

In the end is up to the operator (by configuring such T_heartbeat_timeout) to decide how much time it makes sense to keep existing PDU sessions with the UPF being non-responsive. It's basically a trade-off between rejecting the user or leaving him unattended stating everything is fine while traffic is potentially being dropped.

3- and 4-
Ok so T_hearbeat timeout would be only used  (at the SMF) to move the pfcp fsm state to "will_associate" which should reject new sessions (new procedures actually), while leaving the sessions created until a separate timer  T_release_after (armed upon T_hearbeat times out) triggers, then releasing them.

Then with those 2 timers an operator can control when the UPF is considered in "failure", and after that when the sessions are to be released. If you want to keep them forever, simply do T_release_after=-1 for instance.

I'm fine with keeping emergency ones alive, though not sure if in practice that helps or not so it may make sense to have it configurable.

In any case, all this needs to be implemented and I'm personally not planning to work on this for now, I guess "patches welcome".

5-
Thanks for looking it up. So it is now clear that open5gs-upfd needs to be fixed. Maybe create a separate ticket to follow-up on that one?

6-
I still didn't have time to write the TTCN-3 test for the 5G session, hopefully soon.

Thanks @MrBrownieCGN for the detailed write-up and @pespin for splitting this out into #4876 — the
timer separation and the "make the UPF-failure reaction a choice" direction both match what we see
operationally. A few data points from our side (full 5G stack: UERANSIM gNB/UE over a real NG
interface + eUPF, 8 PDU sessions, default timers, SMF with the merged #4863 change; our pcap and
flow notes are in the comment above).

**Measured sequence (clean run, default timers)**

- T0: UPF stopped
- T0+13.1 s: heartbeat give-up, `No UPF available`
- T0+13.2 s: `OLD Session Will Release` ×8 → Release Command reaches all 8 sessions at the UEs
- T1: UPF started → T1+1.1 s: association restored (`PFCP restoration`) → T1+2.2 s: 8/8 sessions
  re-established (the UEs reactivate and retry until accepted; ~1 reject/s per UE while no UPF is
  associated, same as in your harness)

So the release lands inside the 7.5–18.5 s envelope you derived, and the release + reactivation path
gets everything back ~2 s after the UPF answers again.

**Re your point 6 (`No handler ... gsm-sm.c:759`)**

You are right that the tree differs: at that moment we were running open5gs `f87da618` plus a local
patch stack (we had validated #4863 v2 before it was merged, so line numbers shift twice). I rebuilt
that tree locally: in it `gsm-sm.c:759` is the `default:` branch of
**`smf_gsm_state_wait_5gc_sm_policy_association()`** (function starts at :573; the
`smf_npcf_smpolicycontrol_handle_create() failed` line right before it is :737 of the same function).
So the session the unhandled `OGS_EVENT_SBI_SERVER` arrived for was in
`wait_5gc_sm_policy_association` — exactly the function you identified as having no SBI_SERVER case.
The surrounding log (UPF-down window) shows: repeated PDU-session re-establishment attempts for all
four IMSIs → `No UPFs are PFCP associated that are suited to RR` / `No associated UPF` →
`smpolicycontrol_handle_create() failed` (:737) → then the two unhandled SBI_SERVER events 0.1–0.2 s
apart, which as you suspected were not answered. We did not capture the Nsmf operation name or a
session dump at that moment; if it helps we can re-run that scenario with the incoming operation and
the session state logged.

**One caveat for `action: keep`**

With eUPF the PFCP session table is process memory (restarting the SMF leaves it intact; restarting
the UPF wipes it — measured 8 → 0 sessions). So in the keep branch the SMF has to restore the PFCP
sessions in the UPF unconditionally on re-association (as you describe); otherwise the kept sessions
point at an empty UPF — and we have one observation where retained-but-stale SMF state actively
blocked a UE's re-establishment until we reset the sessions.

Happy to run a prototype of `action: release|keep` through the same test we used for #4863
(stop UPF → wait → start UPF, default timers, 8 sessions over a real NG interface) and report
before/after numbers.

issue.body:
Right now, lots of timer timeout values are calculated/derived based on the same time.message.duration value, which defaults to `local_conf.time.message.duration = ogs_time_from_sec(10)` and can be set through config file:
```
time:
  message:
    duration: 20000
```

This creates problems, since for instance in open5gs-smfd GTPv2C timeout values are set to the same values as PFCP ones, which is IMHO wrong, since in most cases (UE initiated procedures) the GTPv2C procedures will take more time than the PFCP procedures (ie. the later are inner steps of the former).

As a result, while the PFCP procedure is ongoing (or failing at some point), the GTPv2C gtp_xact may have been freed earlier, which means when the inner PGCP procedure finishes (correctly or not), there no way to reach back towards the UE.


In order to fix this, the ogs-config should have proper separation of config fields, one for each timeout, with a sane set of defaults (maybe also defaults tweaked by the application), which can then independently be modified through config file.
Extra logging warning the user can be added if some wrong configured is detected (like the PFCP timeout >= GTPv2C timeout mentioned above).

Maybe I need to pack the NGAP and NGNAS payloads into different SBI messages?

If you could run the scenario without TLS it would be really helpful, ie in open5gs:
```

    server:
      no_tls: true
...

...

@zhangerfei-dp nevermind, I find out thanks to 3GPP TS 23.502 Figure 4.3.4.2-1 that the NGAP and NAS containers need to be sent in 2 different SmUpdateCtx messages.

2. NGAP: {"n2SmInfo":{"contentId":"ngap-sm"},"n2SmInfoType":"PDU_RES_REL_RSP"},

Re T_release_after_upf_failure: our rig can validate it as soon as there's code to test — same procedure

issue.title: [Bug]: SMF PFCP restoration re-installs stale UE IPs after UPF restart (silent downlink black-hole)

issue.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.1 (also observed on main `d6f1ed8`, 2026-10-19)

### Summary

After `docker restart upf` (i.e. UPF process restarts and loses its PFCP state), the SMF's PFCP
**restoration** re-installs the sessions **it holds in memory** — including the UE IPv4 address it
recorded at session creation. If the UE has meanwhile re-registered and received a **new IP**, the
restored downlink PDRs are keyed on the **old** IP, and every downlink packet for the UE's real IP
misses the PDR and is silently black-holed.

On a userspace datapath (eUPF) the effect is a silent drop with **no error log and no drop counter**:
the packet falls through to `XDP_PASS`, hits the kernel, and is discarded as a martian source
(source address does not match the outgoing interface).

### Steps to reproduce (5GC, single UPF, no MPAS)

1. Establish N PDU sessions for N UEs (we use 8 sessions / 4 UEs over a real NG interface:
   UERANSIM gNB+UE, eUPF as UPF, open5gs SMF/AMF/… on the same host).
2. `docker stop upf` → wait for heartbeat give-up → SMF releases all sessions (#4863 path) →
   `docker start upf`.
   *Alternatively* the mismatch also appears when the UE re-registers between the two events.
3. Let the UEs re-register (they get **new** IPs; in our run `10.64.0.2/.3` instead of `10.64.0.64/.65`).
4. Observe: the SMF's restoration re-creates the PFCP sessions, but with the **old** UE IPs.

### Observed behaviour

In the UPF's downlink PDR table (`pdr_map_downlink_ip4` in eUPF; the F-TEID/UE-IP → PDR map):
keys are `10.64.0.64`, `10.64.0.65`, while the UEs' actual tun addresses are `10.64.0.2`, `10.64.0.3`.

eUPF's REST API confirms it received the stale addresses:

```
SEID 4  PDR1 Ipv4 = 10.65.0.65   (while the UE's tun is 10.65.0.2)
```

Download traffic for the real IP then produces (measured, 20 pings from an IMS container):

```
rx_n6  +31     tx_n3  +0       XDP_PASS +46
```

i.e. **the packet never reaches the GTP encapsulation step** — it is passed to the kernel.
Contrast with a UE whose IP did match (same run, same UPF):

```
rx_n6  +38     tx_n3  +20      XDP_REDIRECT +20
```

The whole test took 2 minutes to confirm: a full cold start (`amf+smf → upf → gNB → UE`) makes the
two sides agree again (8 ↔ 8), and every path recovers (ICMP both ways, and `SIP OPTIONS` to the
P-CSCF returns `200 OK`).

### Expected behaviour

Restoration should not resurrect stale UE addressing. Two possible shapes:

1. **Validate on restore**: when re-installing a session, if the UPF-side session state is gone
   (which the SMF can tell from the new Recovery Time Stamp / the fact it is running `pfcp_restoration()`),
   don't blindly re-install the old F-TEID/UE-IP pairs — either refresh them from the current
   SM context or release the session so the UE re-establishes cleanly.
2. **Release instead of restore** when the UPF lost state: this is exactly the "release vs restore"
   decision discussed in #4860 / #4876. If the operator chooses `keep`, the restoration path still
   has to guarantee that the addressing it pushes matches what the UE currently uses.

### Why this matters beyond our rig

* This is the **user-visible failure mode** of the restore/release race in #4860: the control plane
  (and charging) believes the session is alive while the user plane silently drops **all** downlink
  traffic. There is no alarm surface for it.
* It only affects *some* UEs (the ones whose IP changed), so it looks like "random UEs are broken",
  which is very hard to triage — we initially mis-diagnosed it as a NIC/veth problem.
* With #4876 (`T_release_after_upf_failure`) landing, both branches (`release` and `keep`) need this
  invariant: **restoration must use the addressing that the UE actually has now**.

### Logs / evidence

Happy to attach: eUPF `pdr_map_downlink_ip4` dump (bpftool), the two XDP counter deltas above,
the eUPF restoration log line (`session UE 10.64.0.64 -> N3 endpoint …`), and the SMF window
showing the release + restoration. Full analysis and the local guard we added are in our repo;
can share on request.

### Our workaround

A consistency check between the UPF's session UE-IPs and the UEs' actual tunnel addresses, run after
any UPF restart (`session-ip-consistency.sh` in our tree), plus the rule "always do a full cold
start, never restart the UPF alone". Both are workarounds, not fixes.

body:
On the `T_release_after_upf_failure` TODO, a few points from reading main @ 310fea9:

- Where it sits: on `SMF_EVT_N4_NO_HEARTBEAT` the node goes to `will_associate` and `reselect_upf()` runs right away
  (`src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:425-439`). Since #4863 `reselect_upf()` no longer returns when no other UPF is associated
  (`:527-528`), so with a single UPF every session on it is released at that moment. The timer would go between
  those two steps: `will_associate` and rejecting new procedures immediately, the release when it expires.
- Value semantics: `0` = main today, `-1` = never release on this trigger. Note that `-1` is not the same as before
  #4863: before, 5G sessions were already released when another UPF was associated (only the "no UPF left" case kept
  them).
- Session FSM vs. node: a per-node timer (armed at heartbeat give-up, stopped on re-association, runs the existing
  `reselect_upf()` loop on expiry) would leave the session FSMs untouched until it fires; a per-session state as you
  suggest makes it easier to treat sessions differently (e.g. emergency). Either seems fine to us.
- Restoration on re-association: as @zhangerfei-dp measured, a restarted userspace UPF comes back empty. Today
  `pfcp_restoration()` (`:465-506`) runs only when `restoration_required` is set (`:196-198`, `:251-270`, `:279-297`),
  i.e. after a newer Recovery Time Stamp was seen. For sessions kept by the timer it would have to run on every
  re-association of that node, whatever the Recovery Time Stamp says.
- Emergency: `src/smf` has no per-session emergency marker today (two mentions only: `context.c:1670` comment,
  `nsmf-build.c:132`), so an emergency exception would need one first and could come later.
- The UPF-side counterpart is #4877; its "preconfigured time" should not be shorter than this timer.

We are preparing an implementation of `T_release_after_upf_failure` along these lines as a PR against main.

Follow-up on the hold-vs-release question, with measurements, and an offer to implement the configurable variant.

**What we measured** (abts test derived from `simple-test.c`: register, PDU session, pings; then N4 blocked in both directions with iptables on udp/8805 for ~25–30 s while GTP-U stays reachable; NGAP at the gNB and GTP-U replies counted by type):

| Build | After heartbeat gives up (~15 s, phase dependent) | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| main b60aad44 (26f9edd4 + 92655020) | UPF deletes, SMF releases | PDUSessionResourceRelease at the gNB; consistent |
| SMF keeps sessions (old `No UPF available; return` behaviour), UPF b0edf54e | both hold | 38/38 echo replies, 0 NGAP; data path unaffected |
| SMF keeps sessions, UPF with 92655020 | UPF deletes, SMF holds | 22× GTP-U Error Indication, 0 NGAP, **no restoration after re-association** (Recovery Time Stamp unchanged) |

The last row is what an operator gets if `T_release_after_upf_failure` (your TODO in https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/issues/4860#issuecomment-6212762980) is ever added to the SMF alone: the UPF side now deletes immediately, so holding on the SMF side produces a black hole instead of a recovery. 92655020 states the same pairing problem for the SGW-U ("the SGW-C would keep using sessions that no longer exist").

**Why we think the configurable variant is worth having**

1. TS 23.527 §4.3.3: PSA UPF failure without restart is "implementation specific", so both hold and release are conformant on the SMF side. §4.4.3.1 requires the UPF to delete "when ... not reachable for a preconfigured time". The time is free but finite; today's main uses the shortest possible value, and an operator cannot choose a longer one.
2. The common real-life case for a small or single-UPF deployment is a UPF crash followed by a supervisor restart within a few seconds (systemd `Restart=always`). With release-after-heartbeat, every PDU session is torn down a few seconds before the UPF is back and session restoration (§4.3.2) would have worked. For an IMS PDU session this means re-registration and dropped calls.
3. The reverse case, an SMF that is unreachable while the UPF still forwards, now stops user traffic after ~15 s although the data path was healthy (see also the overload case in #4877).

**Proposal** (all keys following the single-key style discussed in #4876, defaults = current main, so nothing changes for anyone who does not opt in):

- SMF: `release_after_upf_failure` seconds. 0 = release when the heartbeat gives up (current). N = keep the sessions for N s and restore them when the UPF comes back; release with "reactivation requested" when the timer expires.
- UPF: `delete_after_smf_failure` seconds (the "preconfigured time" of §4.4.3.1). 0 = current. Documented rule: UPF value ≥ SMF value + heartbeat detection skew, otherwise the two sides disagree.
- Restoration guarded by the PFCP Session Retention Information IE (29.244 §6.2.6.2.1/§6.2.6.2.2): an SMF holding sessions sets PSREI in the Association Setup Request; the UPF retains them if PSREI is set and deletes otherwise; the SMF restores whenever the UPF did not retain, independent of the Recovery Time Stamp. Today neither side implements this IE (`git grep -i retention` in lib/pfcp, src/smf, src/upf is empty).
- AMF: handle PDU Session Resource Notify (TS 23.527 §5.3.3.1, the gNB's reaction to a GTP-U Error Indication) and let the SMF re-establish the PFCP session (§4.3.2). This one is useful on its own: it closes the remaining inconsistency window for any timer choice.

Our extended test case (the table above) would come with the series as a regression test: red for the third row, green for the other two.

If this direction is acceptable, we would send it as two or three PRs (SMF/UPF timers with the coupling rule; retention IE; AMF notify handling). Happy to adjust the key names or the split to your preference first.
@MrBrownieCGN LGTM. I didn't check at the code but as an idea if the release_after timer can be placed in the lib/, it could be named generically "release_after_peer_failure".

Thanks. Agreed — a generic timer in lib/pfcp fits better than two NF-specific ones. Plan for the PR:

- `ogs_pfcp_node_t` gets `t_release_after_peer_failure`, armed when the heartbeat gives up (where `OGS_PFCP_EVT_NO_HEARTBEAT` is raised today) and stopped on re-association. The config key is the same on every PFCP NF: `pfcp: { release_after_peer_failure: <seconds> }`, default 0 = current behaviour (act immediately).
- On expiry lib/pfcp calls back into the NF: SMF/SGW-C release the sessions of that node (with "reactivation requested" where the session type allows it), UPF/SGW-U delete them. Before expiry the NF rejects new procedures for that node and keeps existing sessions, as in the earlier TODO.
- Documented rule in the sample configs: the UPF/SGW-U value should not be shorter than the SMF/SGW-C value plus the heartbeat detection skew, otherwise the two sides disagree.
- Restoration on re-association (Session Retention Information IE) and the AMF handling of PDU Session Resource Notify stay separate commits so each can be reviewed on its own.

Unless you prefer another name or key placement, we will send the lib/pfcp timer first.

issue.title: [PFCP] Add release_after_peer_failure timer and PFCP Session Retention

repository.name: open5gs
repository.description: Open5GS is a C-language Open Source implementation for 5G Core and EPC, i.e. the core network of LTE/NR network (Release-19)

license.name: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0

issue.body:
## Summary

When the PFCP heartbeat towards a peer gives up, the SMF releases all PDU sessions of that UPF at once (`reselect_upf()`, since #4863), and the UPF deletes all sessions of that SMF at once (92655020). As suggested by @pespin in #4860 (https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/issues/4860#issuecomment-6575804663, design agreed in https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/issues/4860#issuecomment-6576234185), this adds a generic lib/pfcp timer, `pfcp.release_after_peer_failure` (seconds, default 0 = current behaviour): it is started when the heartbeat gives up and stopped when the node is associated again. While it runs, the sessions are kept; when it expires, the SMF releases them ("reactivation requested") and the UPF deletes them.

The second commit adds the PFCP Session Retention Information IE (TS 29.244 6.2.6.2), so that both sides agree on which sessions still exist when the association is set up again.

Rebased onto main, which now includes fc26daab9b (only operational sessions are restored after a UPF restart); the restoration in this PR goes through the same `pfcp_restoration()`. The first five commits are #4964 (timer duration 0, `ogs_assert(duration >= 0)` and the validation it needs); this PR will be rebased once #4964 is merged.

## Field motivation

- With the default timers the heartbeat gives up 7.5–18.5 s after the peer stops answering. A UPF that crashes and is restarted within a few seconds, or a short N4 path outage, therefore tears down every PDU session (for IMS: re-registration, dropped calls), although restoration (TS 23.527 4.3.2) or simply the still working data path would have kept them (#4860, comments 6202375701 and 6547687632).
- In an abts-based test with N4 blocked while GTP-U stays reachable (6547687632): both sides holding → 38/38 echo replies and no NGAP; UPF deleting at once while the SMF holds → 22 GTP-U Error Indications and no recovery after re-association. Hence one key for both NFs and a rule for their values.
- #4877: a userspace UPF that deletes on a short SMF stall amplifies the failure.

## Spec

- TS 23.527 4.3.3: "Procedures for PSA UPF failure without restart are implementation specific."
- TS 23.527 4.4.3.1: "When a UPF detects that a peer PFCP entity in the SMF is not reachable for a preconfigured time, ... the UPF shall delete all the session contexts affected by the peer PFCP entity failure that it may have stored."
- TS 23.527 4.5: "If the N4 path to the UPF is down, the SMF should handle this as an UPF Failure without Restart ... If the N4 path to the SMF is down, the UPF should handle this as a SMF Failure without Restart".
- TS 29.244 6.2.6.2.1/6.2.6.2.2, 7.4.4.1 (Table 7.4.4.1-2), 8.2.134 (PSREI), 8.2.135 (CP PFCP Entity IP Address).

## Fix

**`[PFCP] Add release_after_peer_failure timer`**
- lib/pfcp: `release_after_peer_failure` in `ogs_pfcp_context_t` (parsed under `<nf>.pfcp`; any value that fits `ogs_time_t`, invalid values fail the start), `t_release_after_peer_failure` in `ogs_pfcp_node_t`, `ogs_pfcp_node_start_release_after_peer_failure()`. Each NF creates/deletes the timer next to `t_no_heartbeat`. With 0 the timer is started with 0 and expires on the next poll, so the sessions are released right after the current events, as before.
- SMF/UPF: on heartbeat failure the node goes to will_associate as before (no new session selects it); with N > 0 the sessions are kept until the node is associated again or the timer expires. On the SMF, the sessions for which another associated UPF can be selected are released at once ("Reselect UPF"; moving a session to another UPF is not implemented). The timer also bounds the wait after a peer restart (newer Recovery Time Stamp).
- A timer event still queued after re-association, or after the timer was started again, is ignored.
- Sample configs document the key and the rule: the UPF value should not be shorter than the SMF value plus the heartbeat detection skew.

**`[PFCP] Retain kept sessions in Association Setup (TS 29.244 6.2.6.2)`**
- `node->num_of_sessions` counts the sessions bound to the node (`OGS_SETUP_PFCP_NODE()`/`OGS_CLEAR_PFCP_NODE()`). When the node fails with N > 0, the SMF takes `num_of_sessions_kept`. No session is bound to the node meanwhile, so a lower count means that a session was removed and its PFCP Session Deletion may not have reached the UPF; the IE selects the sessions per CP PFCP entity only, so then the SMF does not send it.
- The SMF includes the IE (with its CP PFCP Entity IP Address) while all kept sessions are still there and not yet released on expiry; the UPF retains the sessions of the node and sets PSREI if the IE is present, otherwise deletes them (6.2.6.2.2), also when they are kept in will_associate.
- Only the answer to the last Association Setup Request decides: PSREI set but sessions removed or released since the request was built → a new request without the IE; no PSREI → the kept sessions are restored regardless of the Recovery Time Stamp; sessions released on expiry are neither retained nor restored.
- An association set up by the UPF carries no retention information: the SMF follows with its own request. A node with a pending decision is not selectable, also not through the fallback of the UPF selection.

## Out of scope

- SGW-C/SGW-U: both keep their sessions on heartbeat failure today (comment in 92655020). They follow in a separate PR together (TS 23.007 16.1A.3/16.1A.4); until then they log that the key is ignored.
- AMF handling of PDU Session Resource Notify (TS 23.527 5.3.3.1): separate change, as announced in #4860.
- Retention per CP PFCP entity in the UPF (Open5GS CP functions have a single PFCP entity). If a session was removed during the outage, the kept ones are restored instead of retained, which interrupts their data path briefly.
- PFCP session requests sent to a kept node before it is associated again time out, as during heartbeat detection today.

## Configuration example

```yaml
smf:
  pfcp:
    release_after_peer_failure: 30
upf:
  pfcp:
    release_after_peer_failure: 60
```

## Refs

- Refs #4860 (comments 6575804663 and 6576234185), #4877
- Refs #4876 (separate heartbeat keys would make the detection skew configurable)

## Test plan

- [x] Each of the seven commits builds with `-Dwerror=true` on `main @ d9c44d67f`, and the `core` and `unit` test programs pass on each.
- [x] On the last commit: `tests/pfcp-peer-failure` (6 cases) and the suites registration, vonr, slice, handover, transfer, non3gpp, eir, attach, volte, csfb, 310014 pass.
- [x] `tests/pfcp-peer-failure` (SMF 40 s, UPF 30 s; a peer is made unreachable without a restart with SIGSTOP/SIGCONT; PFCP Session Establishment Requests counted on the metrics server of the UPF): UPF down 25 s then back → PDU session kept and retained, not restored; UPF stays down → released on expiry, no session left in the UPF after the next association; second UPF → released at once, new session on the other UPF; one of two sessions released during the outage → the UPF deletes both, the SMF restores the kept one; released on expiry and the release not answered yet when the UPF comes back → neither retained nor restored (new); SMF stays down → data path keeps working, deleted on expiry.
- [x] With `node->sessions_kept` removed (suggested in review), the second and the new case fail: the UPF keeps the released session after the SMF has removed it.
- [x] `tests/unit/pfcp-retention-test.c`: counting, all kept sessions there (IE), one removed during the failure, also across a second failure (no IE), released on expiry then failed again (no IE), no sessions.
- [ ] Not yet run against a real RAN; @zhangerfei-dp offered to run the stop/start UPF scenario in #4860.

body: Implementation of the timer and the Session Retention handling is in #4959 (two commits: `release_after_peer_failure` in lib/pfcp with SMF and UPF wired up, then the PFCP Session Retention Information IE in Association Setup). SGW-C/SGW-U follow in a separate PR together, as noted in 92655020.
